newsitem.title: USA: GFOA to address yield burning, markups at Fla meet.
newsitem.headline: GFOA to address yield burning, markups at Fla meet.

text.p: GFOA panels will take up draft policies on a number of key issues at the group's annual conference annual conference in Fort Lauderdale, Fla., beginning May 31, including one aimed at curbing alleged "yield burning" in the muni market, the association said.

The Government Finance Officers Association's cash management committee will vote on whether to urge the National Association of Securities Dealers and Securities and Exchange Commission to develop specific standards for markups in government securities.
"The absence of such rules is a contributing factor to the arbitrage yield-burning controversy," GFOA said in a press statement announcing the agenda for the annual conference.
Yield burning refers to allegations that bond underwriters overcharge states and localities for U.S. Treasury securities they bought to help them refinance outstanding bonds.
The IRS has given localities the option of working out closing agreements with the Service on any funds owed in exchange for an IRS pledge that it will not take enforcement action.

NASD says its longstanding rules of fair practice already bar excessive markups of government securities. However, Congress in its 1993 Government Securities Act Amendments authorized NASD to write specific standards on the issue.
NASD published a draft markup rule for comment in summer 1994, but has taken no further action.
GFOA's cash management committee also hopes to develop a recommended practice at the upcoming meeting on electronic transactions for state and local governments.

The group's government debt and fiscal policy panel will discuss the Municipal Securities Rulemaking Board's upcoming rule package aimed at improving public confidence in the muni bond underwriting process.
Also, the panel may back a voluntary effort to improve bondholder communications in the case of defaulted muni securities.
And the panel is set to approve three recommended practices concerning the sale and securitization of property tax liens, use of variable rate debt instruments, and use of taxable muni bonds.
